title: AI Gateway vs. Direct Provider Decision
summary: Decide whether an AI gateway earns its additional trust, latency, cost, and failure boundary through enforceable governance or operational value.
prerequisites: An inventory of applications, providers, models, tools, and data classes
Required identity, policy, resilience, and telemetry controls

sections.title: Require a concrete cross-cutting value
paragraphs: An AI gateway can centralize controls such as authentication, quotas, rate or spend limits, routing, retries, caching, safety policy, logs, and provider abstraction. Direct calls can preserve provider-native behavior, reduce added latency and dependencies, simplify debugging, and limit how many systems can inspect prompts and responses.

Do not add a gateway solely to obtain a unified endpoint. State the policy or operational result it must deliver, then test the exact provider API, model, streaming protocol, modalities, tools, identity, region, transformations, retry behavior, and failure semantics in scope.

The worked case in this module is entirely fictional. Its required gateway value is enforcement of a tenant-wide spend cap plus one joined audit trace for every model request. The gateway qualifies only if applications cannot evade those controls by using provider credentials or an alternate route.
sections.callout: Decision rule: reject a route when any required hard gate is missing or false. Compare weighted scores only among eligible routes.

code.label: Filled fictional decision record
code.code:
SCENARIO STATUS: FICTIONAL TRAINING SCENARIO
Task: Decide whether to adopt a gateway for a fictional support assistant.
Scope: One application, one provider-neutral text model interface, streaming, a read-only lookup tool, a ticket-creation tool, three fictional tenants, one region, and prompts containing internal support data.
Permissions: The application uses workload identity. The selected route holds provider credentials. Gateway administrators can change routes and policies. Audit readers can view metadata and redacted traces. Gateway administrators are not approved to view prompt or response bodies.
Required value: Enforce a tenant-wide spend cap and produce one joined audit trace for each request, including tenant, route, policy result, latency, cost inputs, and outcome.
Enforcement evidence: The fictional gateway rejects requests over the tenant cap; the application process lacks provider credentials; an attempted direct bypass using application credentials fails; accepted requests have trace identifiers joined across the application, gateway, provider adapter, and tool adapter.
Direct baseline: quality 0.90; streaming and tool contracts pass; p95 latency 820 ms; reliability 0.992; normalized cost $0.0044; application and provider traces are joinable.
Gateway result: quality 0.96; streaming and tool contracts pass; p95 latency 910 ms; reliability 0.995; normalized cost $0.0046; gateway, application, provider-adapter, and tool-adapter traces are joinable.
Trust review: Prompt-body retention is not approved; cross-tenant access tests fail safely; direct bypass is blocked; route and policy administration is audited; an outage could affect all three fictional tenants.
Stop conditions: semantic drift, unexpected retention, failed tenant isolation, policy bypass, duplicate side effects, or an unowned single point of failure.
Verification: quality threshold, identity, isolation, retention, streaming, tools, retry and idempotency, bypass, failure injection, load behavior, and end-to-end traces.
Recovery: Freeze gateway changes, disable the affected route, restore the verified direct adapter, retain required controls on the direct path, reconcile requests and writes, and rerun failed tests.
Decision: ADOPT GATEWAY FOR THIS FICTIONAL SCOPE.
Basis: All hard gates pass. The gateway score is 0.7055 and the direct score is 0.6972. This is not a recommendation for any real product.

sections.title: Test the gateway as a new high-value trust boundary
paragraphs: Threat-model credential custody, prompt and response visibility, retention, tenant isolation, policy bypass, transformation drift, caching, fallback behavior, retry duplication, outage blast radius, and administrative access. Compare end-to-end quality, streaming, tool behavior, latency, reliability, observability, and cost with the direct baseline.

Keep provider adapters and contract fixtures portable. A gateway must not erase provider-specific semantics or prevent safe rollback. Gateway bypass must not bypass required identity, tenant, safety, quota, or audit controls.
Every figure below is a hypothetical measured fixture for instruction. It is not a claim about a real provider, model, gateway, product tier, price, latency, reliability, or policy.
sections.callout: Ask who holds provider credentials, who can see content, how long content is retained, how tenants and caches are isolated, whether alternate routes evade policy, and how many workloads a gateway outage affects.

code.label: Fictional measurements and verified arithmetic
code.code:
Request fixture:
  input_tokens = 1000
  output_tokens = 300

Direct fixture:
  quality = 0.90
  p95_latency_ms = 820
  reliability = 0.992
  input_rate_per_1k = 0.0020
  output_rate_per_1k = 0.0080
  request_fee = 0.0000

Gateway fixture:
  quality = 0.96
  p95_latency_ms = 910
  reliability = 0.995
  input_rate_per_1k = 0.0020
  output_rate_per_1k = 0.0080
  request_fee = 0.0002

Normalized cost = input_tokens / 1000 * input_rate_per_1k
                + output_tokens / 1000 * output_rate_per_1k
                + request_fee

Direct cost = 1000/1000 * 0.0020 + 300/1000 * 0.0080 + 0.0000
            = 0.0020 + 0.0024
            = $0.0044

Gateway cost = 1000/1000 * 0.0020 + 300/1000 * 0.0080 + 0.0002
             = 0.0020 + 0.0024 + 0.0002
             = $0.0046

Weighted score = 0.50 * quality
               + 0.20 * (1 - p95_latency_ms / 1000)
               + 0.20 * (1 - normalized_cost / 0.0100)
               + 0.10 * reliability

Direct score = 0.50*0.90 + 0.20*(1-820/1000)
             + 0.20*(1-0.0044/0.0100) + 0.10*0.992
             = 0.4500 + 0.0360 + 0.1120 + 0.0992
             = 0.6972

Gateway score = 0.50*0.96 + 0.20*(1-910/1000)
              + 0.20*(1-0.0046/0.0100) + 0.10*0.995
              = 0.4800 + 0.0180 + 0.1080 + 0.0995
              = 0.7055

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Evidence should include the required value, direct baseline, applicable product and tier capabilities, trust and data review, exact API compatibility, quality evaluation, contract fixtures, latency and cost results, failure injection, policy enforcement, an owner, a decision expiry, and a tested exit route.

The fictional quality gate means that each route passed the predetermined minimum on the same evaluation set. The API gates cover streaming boundaries, tool names and arguments, identity, tenant isolation, retention, retry and idempotency behavior, and bypass prevention. A failed or absent gate denies a route before numeric scoring.

A passing simulator fixture does not prove that a real product enforces a policy. Real adoption requires dated product documentation, configuration inspection, contract tests, failure injection, load tests, access review, and an end-to-end trace. The linked Azure and Cloudflare documentation provides first-party product references, but those links could not be rechecked while drafting. Their recorded verification dates are preserved and are not evidence of a new review.
sections.callout: Stop on semantic drift, unexpected sensitive-content retention, failed isolation, policy bypass, unsafe retry duplication, or loss of an owned recovery route.

Required hard gates for each candidate route:

  tenant_isolation_tested
  prompt_retention_approved

Original fictional decision:
  ADOPT GATEWAY
  Both routes pass every hard gate.
  Gateway score 0.7055 exceeds direct score 0.6972.

Stop and exit rehearsal:
1. Freeze new gateway configuration changes.
2. Disable the affected gateway route or policy.
3. Restore the tested direct adapter using credentials held outside the gateway.
4. Keep required identity, tenant, safety, quota, and audit controls active on the direct route.
5. Reconcile request state and side-effecting tool writes using idempotency keys.
6. Compare direct and gateway traces.
7. Re-enable the gateway only after the failed evidence and contract tests pass.

sections.title: File: evaluator.py
paragraphs: Save this complete standard-library evaluator as evaluator.py. It validates the fixture, request, and every route before calculating any cost or score. A malformed numeric field makes the fixture ineligible and produces a nonzero exit status. A missing or false hard gate still denies only that route, preserving the existing hard-gate behavior.

Token counts use the exercise contract of nonnegative integers. Booleans, fractions, negative integers, strings, and nonfinite floating-point values are rejected. Rates, fees, and latency must be nonnegative finite numbers. Quality and reliability must be finite numbers in the inclusive interval 0 through 1.

These bounds are requirements of this exercise, not claimed universal standards for AI gateway metrics. Why quality and reliability must use this particular interval outside the supplied scoring contract is UNKNOWN. Establishing broader bounds would require the specification for the real evaluation and reliability metrics. Python documents math.isfinite at https://docs.python.org/3/library/math.html#math.isfinite and documents that bool is a subclass of int at https://docs.python.org/3/library/functions.html#bool, which is why Boolean rejection is explicit.
sections.callout: Validation precedes scoring. Negative token counts can no longer create artificial negative cost or a higher score, and missing hard gates continue to produce route-level DENY results.

sections.title: Changed-input answer key
paragraphs: The decision reverses to direct. The gateway fails prompt_retention_approved and is denied before scoring. The direct route still passes every gate, so it remains eligible and is selected.

The gateway measurements did not change, so its mathematical score would still be 0.7055. That score does not participate in route selection because the gateway is ineligible. The trace is: inspect gates, deny gateway for failed retention evidence, score the eligible direct route, select direct.
sections.callout: Expected changed decision: USE DIRECT. This reversal demonstrates that trust and API-contract gates constrain optimization rather than becoming small score penalties.

sections.title: File: verify_exercise.py
paragraphs: Save this complete standard-library assertion runner as verify_exercise.py. It preserves the exact expected stdout and decisions for every original fixture. It also generates temporary negative cases without modifying the supplied fixture files.

The added cases cover negative, fractional, and Boolean token counts; every rate, fee, and latency field below zero; both sides of the quality and reliability bounds; malformed request, routes, and route structures; and a missing required numeric field. The original nonfinite-latency fixture continues to exercise math.isfinite. The generated missing-gate case continues to deny the gateway for absent bypass_blocked while allowing and selecting direct.
The final success line remains expected output pending learner execution. This replacement does not claim that the verifier was executed while drafting.
sections.callout: Each invalid numeric or structural case must exit nonzero before printing a route decision. A missing hard gate is different: it denies that route, and another valid eligible route can still be selected.

code.label: verify_exercise.py
code.code:
import copy
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
EVALUATOR = os.path.join(ROOT, "evaluator.py")


def run(path):
    completed = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, EVALUATOR, path],
        cwd=ROOT,
        text=True,
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )
    return completed.returncode, completed.stdout, completed.stderr


def assert_case(path, expected_status, expected_stdout):
    status, stdout, stderr = run(os.path.join(ROOT, path))
    assert status == expected_status, (
        f"{path}: status {status}, expected {expected_status}; stderr={stderr!r}"
    )
    assert stdout == expected_stdout, (
        f"{path}: stdout mismatch\nEXPECTED:\n{expected_stdout!r}\n"
        f"ACTUAL:\n{stdout!r}\nSTDERR:\n{stderr!r}"
    )
    assert stderr == "", f"{path}: unexpected stderr: {stderr!r}"


def write_and_run(directory, filename, fixture):
    path = os.path.join(directory, filename)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(fixture, handle)
    return run(path)


def assert_generated_error(directory, filename, fixture, expected_stdout):
    status, stdout, stderr = write_and_run(directory, filename, fixture)
    assert status == 1, (
        f"{filename}: status {status}, expected 1; stderr={stderr!r}"
    )
    assert stdout == expected_stdout, (
        f"{filename}: stdout mismatch\nEXPECTED:\n{expected_stdout!r}\n"
        f"ACTUAL:\n{stdout!r}\nSTDERR:\n{stderr!r}"
    )
    assert stderr == "", f"{filename}: unexpected stderr: {stderr!r}"


def changed(base, path, value):
    fixture = copy.deepcopy(base)
    target = fixture
    for key in path[:-1]:
        target = target[key]
    target[path[-1]] = value
    return fixture


def without(base, path):
    fixture = copy.deepcopy(base)
    target = fixture
    for key in path[:-1]:
        target = target[key]
    del target[path[-1]]
    return fixture


def main():
    assert_case(
        "fixtures/original.json",
        0,
        "decision=gateway\n"
        "direct: ALLOW score=0.6972 cost=$0.0044 latency_p95_ms=820.0\n"
        "gateway: ALLOW score=0.7055 cost=$0.0046 latency_p95_ms=910.0\n",
    )
    assert_case(
        "fixtures/changed-retention.json",
        0,
        "decision=direct\n"
        "direct: ALLOW score=0.6972 cost=$0.0044 latency_p95_ms=820.0\n"
        "gateway: DENY (failed=prompt_retention_approved)\n",
    )
    assert_case(
        "fixtures/malformed.json",
        1,
        "ERROR: input_tokens: expected finite number\n",
    )
    assert_case(
        "fixtures/nonfinite.json",
        1,
        "ERROR: p95_latency_ms: expected finite number\n",
    )
    assert_case(
        "fixtures/bool.json",
        1,
        "ERROR: quality: expected finite number\n",
    )

    original_path = os.path.join(ROOT, "fixtures", "original.json")
    with open(original_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        original = json.load(handle)

    negative_cases = [
        (
            "negative-input-tokens.json",
            changed(original, ["request", "input_tokens"], -1000),
            "ERROR: input_tokens: expected nonnegative integer\n",
        ),
        (
            "fractional-output-tokens.json",
            changed(original, ["request", "output_tokens"], 300.5),
            "ERROR: output_tokens: expected nonnegative integer\n",
        ),
        (
            "bool-input-tokens.json",
            changed(original, ["request", "input_tokens"], True),
            "ERROR: input_tokens: expected finite number\n",
        ),
        (
            "negative-input-rate.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "input_rate_per_1k"], -0.001),
            "ERROR: input_rate_per_1k: expected nonnegative finite number\n",
        ),
        (
            "negative-output-rate.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "output_rate_per_1k"], -0.001),
            "ERROR: output_rate_per_1k: expected nonnegative finite number\n",
        ),
        (
            "negative-request-fee.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "request_fee"], -0.001),
            "ERROR: request_fee: expected nonnegative finite number\n",
        ),
        (
            "negative-latency.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "p95_latency_ms"], -1),
            "ERROR: p95_latency_ms: expected nonnegative finite number\n",
        ),
        (
            "quality-below-zero.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "quality"], -0.01),
            "ERROR: quality: expected number in range 0..1\n",
        ),
        (
            "quality-above-one.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "quality"], 1.01),
            "ERROR: quality: expected number in range 0..1\n",
        ),
        (
            "reliability-below-zero.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "reliability"], -0.01),
            "ERROR: reliability: expected number in range 0..1\n",
        ),
        (
            "reliability-above-one.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct", "reliability"], 1.01),
            "ERROR: reliability: expected number in range 0..1\n",
        ),
        (
            "request-not-object.json",
            changed(original, ["request"], []),
            "ERROR: request: expected object\n",
        ),
        (
            "routes-not-object.json",
            changed(original, ["routes"], []),
            "ERROR: routes: expected object\n",
        ),
        (
            "route-not-object.json",
            changed(original, ["routes", "direct"], []),
            "ERROR: route direct: expected object\n",
        ),
        (
            "missing-quality.json",
            without(original, ["routes", "direct", "quality"]),
            "ERROR: route direct: missing required field quality\n",
        ),
    ]

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        for filename, fixture, expected_stdout in negative_cases:
            assert_generated_error(
                directory,
                filename,
                fixture,
                expected_stdout,
            )

        missing_gate = without(
            original,
            ["routes", "gateway", "bypass_blocked"],
        )
        status, stdout, stderr = write_and_run(
            directory,
            "missing-gate.json",
            missing_gate,
        )

    assert status == 0, f"missing gate case status={status}; stderr={stderr!r}"
    assert stdout == (
        "decision=direct\n"
        "direct: ALLOW score=0.6972 cost=$0.0044 latency_p95_ms=820.0\n"
        "gateway: DENY (missing=bypass_blocked)\n"
    ), f"missing gate case stdout mismatch: {stdout!r}"
    assert stderr == "", f"missing gate case unexpected stderr: {stderr!r}"
    print("all assertions passed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

sections.title: Behavior assertions and numeric-domain interpretation
paragraphs: The original worked case remains unchanged. Both routes pass every hard gate, direct cost is $0.0044, gateway cost is $0.0046, the respective scores are 0.6972 and 0.7055, and gateway is selected. The independent changed-input case also remains unchanged: failed gateway retention evidence produces a gateway DENY before score comparison, leaving direct as the selected route.

The defect accepted input_tokens=-1000. With the direct rates, that invalid count produces -1000/1000 * 0.0020 + 300/1000 * 0.0080 = $0.0004. Substitution into the supplied scoring formula raises the direct score from 0.6972 to 0.7772. Those calculations describe the defect, not a valid result. The replacement rejects the count before either cost or score is calculated.

Counts represent discrete token quantities in this exercise, so their declared domain is nonnegative integers. Rates, fees, and latency cannot be negative under the exercise contract and must be finite so arithmetic produces supported rendered fields. Quality and reliability are normalized exercise inputs, so values below 0 or above 1 are rejected rather than rewarded or penalized by extrapolation.

Fixture, request, routes, and route objects are checked before scoring. Every route must contain the numeric fields needed to render score, cost, and latency. Missing hard gates remain route-level evidence failures rather than malformed-fixture errors. Thus an absent bypass_blocked field yields DENY for that route exactly as before, while an absent quality field makes the fixture malformed and prevents any eligibility decision.

No actual execution is claimed. The original and added stdout strings are expected results derived from the code and supplied fictional inputs. Running python3 verify_exercise.py is what would establish whether the assertions pass in a learner's local Python environment.
sections.callout: Domain validation protects the decision trace: validate structure, validate numeric domains, evaluate hard gates, score only eligible routes, then select the highest eligible score.

code.label: Validation and decision trace
code.code:
DECLARED EXERCISE DOMAINS
input_tokens, output_tokens:
  nonnegative integers
  reject Boolean values, fractions, strings, negative values, and nonfinite floats

input_rate_per_1k, output_rate_per_1k, request_fee, p95_latency_ms:
  nonnegative finite numbers
  reject Boolean values, strings, negative values, NaN, and positive or negative infinity

quality, reliability:
  finite numbers in the inclusive range 0..1
  reject Boolean values, strings, values outside the range, NaN, and infinity

DECISION ORDER
1. Require a fixture object containing a request object and a nonempty routes object.
2. Require token fields and all numeric route fields.
3. Validate every numeric value against its declared domain.
4. For each route, deny it if a required hard gate is missing or is not exactly true.
5. Calculate cost and score only for routes that pass every hard gate.
6. Select the eligible route with the highest score.
7. If no route is eligible, exit nonzero with ERROR: no eligible route.

TRACE FOR THE INVALID NEGATIVE-COUNT CASE
Supplied invalid input_tokens: -1000
Old direct cost: -1000/1000*0.0020 + 300/1000*0.0080 = 0.0004
Old direct score: 0.50*0.90 + 0.20*(1-820/1000)
                + 0.20*(1-0.0004/0.0100) + 0.10*0.992
                = 0.7772
Patched result: ERROR: input_tokens: expected nonnegative integer
Eligibility decision: none, because malformed input is rejected before scoring.

TRACE FOR THE CHANGED RETENTION CASE
Request and route numeric domains: valid
Direct hard gates: all true
Gateway prompt_retention_approved: false
Gateway result: DENY before scoring
Direct score: 0.6972
Final decision: direct

STATUS
All displayed command results are expected output pending execution.
No provider, gateway, network, or external package is used.

sections.title: Transfer the method without assuming feature equivalence
paragraphs: Apply the method separately when evaluating Meta or Llama offerings, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, and Z.ai. A model-family name does not identify one universal serving API or policy. For each actual serving provider and gateway tier, record the exact endpoint, authentication method, model identifier, region, streaming protocol, tool schema, content transformations, retry rules, idempotency behavior, retention terms, and dated price source.

Provider-neutral means the decision fields and tests can transfer. It does not mean APIs, features, security controls, limits, quality, latency, reliability, retention, or prices are equivalent. Current provider-specific prices and feature outcomes for all named families are UNKNOWN in this module. Establish them with dated first-party API, policy, pricing, and product documentation plus measurements from the precise route under evaluation.

Azure API Management and Cloudflare AI Gateway are examples with first-party gateway documentation listed in the sources. No result from the fictional simulator should be attributed to either product. The source links could not be network-verified during this drafting pass, so their recorded lastVerified dates remain historical metadata rather than a new confirmation.
sections.callout: A unified endpoint is not evidence of compatibility. Preserve native contract fixtures and a tested direct adapter. Any bypass or rollback path must continue enforcing required controls.

code.label: Provider-specific evidence checklist
code.code:
For each serving provider, model, region, gateway product, and tier, attach:
- dated first-party capability, API, policy, limit, and pricing documentation
- exact endpoint, authentication method, model identifier, and region
- identity and provider-credential custody review
- tenant-isolation and cache-isolation tests
- prompt and response visibility, logging, and retention review
- quality evaluation against the stated minimum
- streaming-boundary, error-mapping, and tool-schema fixtures
- retry, fallback, and idempotency failure-injection results
- direct and gateway quality, p95 latency, reliability, normalized cost, and trace results
- bypass tests proving required controls remain enforced
- outage blast-radius analysis
- owner, review date, stop conditions, and tested rollback route

Record UNKNOWN or deny the route when required evidence is absent. Do not infer feature or pricing equivalence across Meta/Llama, Qwen, DeepSeek, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, or their serving providers.

sections.title: ASSUMPTIONS.
paragraphs: Python 3.9 or later is available through the python3 command. The fictional quality gate represents a predetermined minimum evaluated consistently for both routes. The fictional rates, measurements, controls, and test outcomes are teaching inputs rather than observations about a real service. The supplied source metadata and verification dates were required to remain unchanged. No gateway administrator is approved to view fictional prompt or response bodies.

sections.title: OMITTED.
paragraphs: Nothing requested was intentionally omitted. Real provider prices, current provider-specific feature results, policy guarantees, and actual execution results are not supplied because they were not established by the provided evidence. They are explicitly marked UNKNOWN or expected pending execution rather than estimated.
